S1::what % of customers r repeat custome.sql:
WITH valid_orders AS (
  SELECT o.order_id, c.customer_unique_id
  FROM orders o
  JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
  WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
),
per_customer AS (
  SELECT customer_unique_id, COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS order_count
  FROM valid_orders
  GROUP BY customer_unique_id
)
SELECT
  100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN order_count >= 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS repeat_customer_pct
FROM per_customer;
S1::what % of customers r repeat custome.explanation: Shares of customers (unique customer_unique_id) with 2 or more valid orders out of all customers with at least one valid order, returned as a percentage.
assumptions: Customer = customers.customer_unique_id
Valid order = order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable'), over all time
Percentage requested, so the share is multiplied by 100

S4::what % of customers r repeat custome.sql:
WITH valid_orders AS (
  SELECT o.order_id, c.customer_unique_id
  FROM orders o
  JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
  WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
),
cust_counts AS (
  SELECT customer_unique_id, COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS n_orders
  FROM valid_orders
  GROUP BY customer_unique_id
)
SELECT
  100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN n_orders >= 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS repeat_customer_pct
FROM cust_counts;
S4::what % of customers r repeat custome.explanation: Percentage of customers (unique customers) who placed 2 or more valid orders over all time.
assumptions: Customer = COUNT(DISTINCT customers.customer_unique_id)
Repeat customer = customer_unique_id with 2+ valid orders (order_status NOT IN ('canceled','unavailable'))
All-time period (no date range given)
Result returned as a percentage (0-100) since the question asked for %

S1::number of currently active sellers i.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT oi.seller_id) AS active_sellers
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
  AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= TIMESTAMP '2018-06-02'
  AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < TIMESTAMP '2018-09-01'
  AND LOWER(p.category_en) IN ('cool_stuff', 'cool stuff');
S1::number of currently active sellers i.explanation: Counts distinct sellers with at least one order item in the cool_stuff category on a valid order purchased between 2018-06-02 and 2018-08-31 inclusive, per the active-seller definition.
assumptions: "Currently active" uses the active-seller rule: at least one order_item on a valid order (status not canceled/unavailable) purchased 2018-06-02 to 2018-08-31 inclusive
Category matched on products.category_en ('cool_stuff', the English name for the cool_stuff category; space/underscore variants accepted)
Filter applied on order_purchase_timestamp

S4::whats the late delivery rate by cust.sql:
SELECT r.region,
       SUM(CASE WHEN CAST(o.order_delivered_customer_date AS DATE) > CAST(o.order_estimated_delivery_date AS DATE) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)::DOUBLE
         / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS late_rate
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
JOIN regions r ON r.state = c.customer_state
WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'
  AND o.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
  AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= TIMESTAMP '2018-07-01'
  AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < TIMESTAMP '2018-08-01'
GROUP BY r.region
ORDER BY late_rate DESC;
S4::whats the late delivery rate by cust.explanation: Late delivery rate (late delivered orders / delivered orders with a delivery date) for orders purchased in July 2018, grouped by the customer's region.
assumptions: "Last month" = July 2018, filtered on order_purchase_timestamp
Late rate = orders with delivered_customer_date > estimated_delivery_date, divided by delivered orders with a non-null delivery date, per the business rules
Region is the customer's region via customers.customer_state joined to regions
Rate returned as a fraction between 0 and 1
